title: Leadership and management
blurb: Define leadership and management as PRINCE2 7 does, tell them apart in practice, and explain why temporary project teams need both.
question: A project manager issues a work package and then spends time persuading a reluctant department head to release two specialists. Which action is management and which is leadership?

teach.h: Two different jobs inside every project role
teach.body: Formally, leadership is motivating people to achieve the project's objectives: persuading, influencing and co-creating with a focus on key relationships, and seeking regular feedback so people stay aligned. Management is instructing the execution of tasks in line with agreed ways of working. In plain English: leadership gets people to want to go somewhere together; management makes sure the agreed work gets done the agreed way.

rows.label: How
values: In line with agreed ways of working

teach.caption: Both definitions come from manual 3.3. Learn the trigger words: 'motivate, influence, co-create' versus 'instruct tasks'.

head: Strand
What it looks like
rows: Linking the work to the project's objectives
Designing products and ways of working together
teach.caption: On projects, leadership is best done through collaboration across the project ecosystem.

teach.h: Why temporary teams need a different style
teach.body: A project team is temporary and usually crosses organizational boundaries. PRINCE2 notes that a temporary leader can find it harder to exercise authority, and that it is not unusual for team members to be more senior than the project manager. So the project manager cannot simply rely on position. Influence, co-creation and good relationships carry more weight than in an established business team.

root.label: Look at what the person is doing

children.label: Management
children.sub: tasks done in line with agreed ways of working

teach.h: Both live in the same roles
teach.body: PRINCE2 does not hand leadership to one person and management to another. The role descriptions mix both. The project manager delegates work and sets work package tolerances, but also manages relationships within the project ecosystem and supports the team's safety and well-being. Team managers and the project board carry a similar blend at their own level.

teach.h: Management and leadership sides of three roles
head: Role
Management side
Leadership side
teach.caption: Paraphrased from the PRINCE2 7 role descriptions (Quick Reference Guide).

teach.body: Project manager Tomasz Novak is replacing Fernmoor's paper bin-collection rounds with a route app. Senior engineer Grace Adeyemi, two grades above him, leads the build team. Tomasz manages: he issues work packages with tolerances and expects the agreed testing procedure to be followed. He also leads: he explains how the app will cut missed collections, co-creates the team's ways of working with Grace, and asks for feedback every fortnight. Grace follows the procedures willingly because she helped shape them.

teach.text: Do not file 'instructing the execution of tasks in line with agreed ways of working' under leadership: that is the PRINCE2 definition of management. And do not assume leadership belongs to the project board alone: the project manager and team managers lead too.

items: Leadership: motivating people towards objectives by persuading, influencing and co-creating, focused on key relationships, with regular feedback (manual 3.3).
Management: instructing the execution of tasks in line with agreed ways of working (manual 3.3).
On projects, leadership is best done through collaboration across the project ecosystem.
Temporary teams need a different style: authority is harder to exercise and team members may be more senior than the project manager.
Each role description blends management and leadership responsibilities.

summary: You can now define leadership and management in PRINCE2 7 terms and classify an action as one or the other. You can also explain why temporary project teams, where the project manager may be junior to team members, depend on influence and co-creation as well as instruction.

A.q: Which statement describes management as PRINCE2 7 defines it?
options: Motivating people to work towards the project's objectives
Persuading and influencing people through key relationships
Instructing the execution of tasks in line with agreed ways of working
Making decisions at the most local level where the knowledge resides
A.why: PRINCE2 7 defines management as instructing the execution of tasks in line with agreed ways of working (manual 3.3).

whyNot.0: Motivating people towards the project's objectives is part of the definition of leadership.
whyNot.1: Persuading and influencing with a focus on key relationships is part of leadership.
whyNot.3: Deciding at the most local level where the knowledge resides is how the people element applies manage by exception.

A.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. In PRINCE2 7, [?] includes motivating, persuading, influencing and co-creating, with a focus on key relationships.
options: leadership
management
assurance
governance
A.why: These are the elements of leadership in manual 3.3.

whyNot.1: Management is instructing the execution of tasks in line with agreed ways of working.
whyNot.2: Assurance is about independently checking the project's performance and products on behalf of the board.
whyNot.3: Governance concerns the rules and constraints for directing the project, not the personal skills of motivating and influencing.

A.q: Why do project teams usually need a different style of leadership and management from established business teams?
options: The business layer directs the team members' daily tasks
Project teams are smaller, so leadership adds little value
Team members report directly to the project board
Temporary leaders can find authority harder to exercise
A.why: Project teams are temporary and cross organizational boundaries, so a temporary leader or manager can find it harder to exercise authority (manual 3.3).

whyNot.0: The business layer commissions the project and sets project tolerances; it does not direct team members' daily work.
whyNot.1: PRINCE2 stresses leadership on projects; size is not the reason given for a different style.
whyNot.2: Team members work to team managers and the project manager, who works on behalf of the board.

B.q:
Which two statements about leadership in PRINCE2 7 are correct?
1. Leadership includes seeking regular feedback so that people stay aligned to the objectives.
2. Leadership is defined as instructing tasks in line with agreed ways of working.
3. On projects, leadership is best done through collaboration across the project ecosystem.
4. Leadership is a duty of the project board rather than of the project manager.
options: 1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
3 and 4
B.why: Seeking regular feedback is part of leadership (1), and PRINCE2 says leadership on projects is best done through collaboration across the project ecosystem (3).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is the definition of management, not leadership.
whyNot.2: Statement 2 defines management, and statement 4 is false because project managers and team managers also lead.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is false: leadership is needed in every project role, including the project manager's.

B.q: A project manager's team includes a senior analyst who is two grades above her in the organization. Which statement reflects PRINCE2 guidance?
options: The analyst should join the project board to reflect seniority
The executive should instruct the analyst instead of the project manager
The analyst should be swapped for someone junior to the PM
This is not unusual, so she leads through influence and collaboration
B.why: PRINCE2 notes it is not unusual for team members to be more senior than the project manager, so leadership through influence and collaboration matters (manual 3.3).

whyNot.0: Board membership depends on representing business, user or supplier interests and having authority, not on grade.
whyNot.1: The project manager runs the project day to day on the board's behalf; passing instruction to the executive undermines that role.
whyNot.2: Roles should reflect capability, authority and availability; a capable senior analyst is not a problem to remove.

B.q: Which activity is an example of management rather than leadership?
options: Issuing a work package to be done in line with agreed procedures
Asking team members for regular feedback on their alignment
Persuading a department head to release two specialists
Explaining to the team how the project will improve patient care
B.why: Instructing the execution of tasks in line with agreed ways of working is management (manual 3.3).

whyNot.1: Seeking regular feedback to keep people aligned is part of leadership.
whyNot.2: Persuading someone you cannot instruct is influencing, which is leadership.
whyNot.3: Linking the work to the project's objectives motivates people, which is leadership.

C.q: A project manager issues a work package that sets out the procedures the team must follow, then holds fortnightly conversations to check the team still sees why the work matters. Which statement is correct?
options: Both actions are leadership, as both involve the team manager
Both actions are management, as both happen within a stage
Issuing the work is management; the conversations are leadership
Issuing the work is leadership; the conversations are management
C.why: Instructing tasks in line with agreed ways of working is management; motivating and seeking regular feedback to keep people aligned is leadership (manual 3.3).

whyNot.0: Who is involved does not decide the category: instructing tasks is management.
whyNot.1: Timing within a stage does not decide the category: seeking feedback to keep people aligned is leadership.

C.q: Which project manager responsibility in the PRINCE2 7 role description is about relationships rather than task control?
options: Setting work package tolerances for team managers
Managing relationships within the project ecosystem
Delegating work to team managers or team members
Making sure decisions follow the board's guidance
C.why: The project manager's role description includes managing relationships within the project ecosystem, the leadership side of the role.

whyNot.0: Setting work package tolerances is a control over the work, the management side of the role.
whyNot.2: Delegating work is part of directing tasks, the management side of the role.
whyNot.3: Keeping decisions in line with board guidance and tolerances is a control responsibility.

C.q: A project manager co-creates the team's ways of working with team members before instructing work in line with them. What does PRINCE2 say this achieves?
options: It removes the need for the board to direct the project
It replaces the need for work package tolerances
It moves accountability for the work to the team
It makes people more willing to be managed in line with them
C.why: Co-creating ways of working with team members and stakeholders significantly improves people's willingness to be managed in line with them (manual 3.3, as cited in the official Practitioner rationales).

whyNot.0: The project board still directs the project; co-creation does not change the levels of organization.
whyNot.1: Work package tolerances are still set by the project manager to enable management by exception.
whyNot.2: Co-creation builds ownership but does not transfer accountability defined in the role descriptions.

reteach.title: The head chef
reteach.question: What does a good head chef do besides telling cooks which dishes to prepare?

blocks.body: A head chef tells each cook which dishes to prepare and expects the agreed recipes to be followed: that is management. The same chef also inspires the brigade, wins over a sceptical owner, designs new dishes with the cooks and asks how service felt: that is leadership. A visiting chef running a pop-up kitchen with strangers needs far more of the second hat.

rows.label: Example
values: Designing a menu with the cooks

blocks.text: A pop-up kitchen is like a project team: temporary, mixed and sometimes full of people more senior than the chef in charge. Authority alone will not carry it.

explain.body: Leadership is motivating people towards the project's objectives: persuading, influencing and co-creating with a focus on key relationships, and seeking regular feedback to keep people aligned.

test.q: Which is part of PRINCE2's description of leadership?
options: Seeking regular feedback to keep people aligned
Instructing tasks in line with agreed ways of working
Recording progress against the stage plan
Approving work package tolerances for each team
test.why: Seeking regular feedback so people remain aligned to the objectives is part of leadership (manual 3.3).

whyNot.1: Instructing tasks in line with agreed ways of working is management.
whyNot.2: Recording progress is a control activity under the progress practice.
whyNot.3: Setting work package tolerances is a project manager control, not part of the leadership definition.

explain.body: Management is instructing the execution of tasks in line with agreed ways of working. It assumes the ways of working are already agreed; leadership is often how they get agreed.

test.q: A team manager tells a developer to run the agreed regression tests before each release. What is this an example of?
options: Co-creation
Leadership
Management
Social cohesion
test.why: Instructing a task to be executed in line with agreed ways of working is management.

whyNot.0: Co-creation would involve designing products or ways of working together, not instructing an agreed task.
whyNot.1: Leadership is motivating, persuading, influencing and co-creating.
whyNot.3: Social cohesion is built by people meeting purposefully and regularly to build trust.

explain.body: Project teams are temporary and cross organizational boundaries. A temporary leader can find authority harder to exercise, and team members may be more senior than the project manager.

test.q: Which statement about authority in project teams is correct?
options: The project manager is the most senior member of the team
It can be harder for a temporary leader to exercise authority
Team members' line managers direct the project's daily work
Authority in a project team comes from grade in the business
test.why: PRINCE2 notes that a temporary leader or manager can find it more challenging to exercise authority (manual 3.3).

whyNot.0: PRINCE2 says it is not unusual for team members to be more senior than the project manager.
whyNot.2: Day-to-day management of the project sits with the project manager on behalf of the board.
whyNot.3: Project authority comes from the role descriptions and delegated tolerances, not grade.

explain.body: PRINCE2 role descriptions blend the two. The project manager delegates work and sets tolerances (management) and manages relationships within the project ecosystem (leadership). The board sets stage tolerances and supports social cohesion.

test.q: Which project board responsibility shows the leadership side of directing?
options: Setting stage tolerances
Approving the change budget
Authorizing each stage
Supporting social cohesion
test.why: The board's role description includes monitoring and supporting social cohesion within the project ecosystem, a people and relationships responsibility.

whyNot.0: Setting stage tolerances is a control that enables management by exception.
whyNot.1: Approving the change budget is a control over changes to the baseline.
whyNot.2: Authorizing stages is a decision and control point.
